message.content:
**Pantone “Sky Blue” – common reference**

| Pantone Code | Description | Approx. CMYK | Approx. RGB |
|--------------|-------------|--------------|-------------|
| **Pantone 14‑4318 TPU** | “Sky Blue” (Pantone’s own name for a bright, airy blue) | C 0 M 0 Y 30 K 0 | R 135 G 206 B 235 |
| **Pantone 14‑4318 C** | Same hue in the Pantone Coated (C) series | C 0 M 0 Y 30 K 0 | R 135 G 206 B 235 |
| **Pantone 14‑4318 U** | Same hue in the Pantone Uncoated (U) series | C 0 M 0 Y 30 K 0 | R 135 G 206 B 235 |

> **Note:** Pantone’s “Sky Blue” is officially identified as **Pantone 14‑4318**.  
> The code is the same across the coated (C), uncoated (U), and textile (TPU) series, but the appearance can vary slightly depending on the substrate.

---

### Other “sky‑blue” options in Pantone

| Pantone Code | Name (Pantone) | Typical Use |
|--------------|----------------|-------------|
| **Pantone 13‑4318 C** | “Light Sky Blue” | Light, airy designs; often used in fashion and interior paint. |
| **Pantone 15‑4318 C** | “Bright Sky Blue” | Brighter, more saturated sky‑blue; good for logos and signage. |
| **Pantone 14‑4318 C** | “Sky Blue” | Classic, balanced sky‑blue. |
| **Pantone 14‑4318 U** | “Sky Blue” | Same hue, but on uncoated paper or textiles. |

If you’re working with a specific medium (e.g., digital, print, textile), let me know and I can give you the most appropriate Pantone reference and its closest RGB/CMYK equivalents.
